     "subtitle": "Jubilee 202nd episode, Zagreb motifs and sponsor support",
     "screenshot_description": "Host Khan shows the design on his black T-shirt with motifs of the Lotrščak tower and Dubrava.",
     "content": "The new, 202nd episode of **Ril Tok Podcast** begins in the relaxed atmosphere of the new studio, where hosts **Khan** and **Doktor Oga** greet the viewers. **Doktor Oga** appears in a completely black outfit (*all black*), while **Khan** proudly shows off a black T-shirt from the domestic brand Grič, whose back design combines recognizable Zagreb motifs like the Lotrščak tower and the Grič cannon with symbols of Dubrava.\n\nUnlike the first episode of the new season, when there was stress regarding the technical correctness of the cameras and microphones, the hosts point out that they are now completely relaxed. **Doktor Oga** mentions that this season he consumes exclusively non-alcoholic versions of cocktails, while **Khan** jokingly takes on the traditional podcaster burden of trying out sponsor drinks and food.\n\nBefore introducing the guests themselves, the hosts took time to thank the numerous partners and sponsors who support the podcast's work:\n- **Dominos** and **Wolt** for the delivery of food and pizzas that the crew enjoyed before filming.\n- **Vending Hub** vending machines with a wide selection of drinks and unusual sweets in Zagreb and Sveta Nedelja.\n- **Punch Club** organic cocktails and **Monster** energy drinks.\n- **Doktor Urban** (in whose premises at Ilica 45 and in Malešnica the podcast is filmed) and **Garica** (CBD products in Zagreb and Split).\n- **Barbershop Šefa** in Dubrava and the newly opened pub **Pomalo** in Ozaljska Street, whose craft beers (*Dubrovnik Lager* and *Pomalo Gipsy Pale Ale*) the guests and hosts drank during the show.\n\n**Doktor Oga** also reminded viewers about PayPal donations aimed at buying a new camera for host Matija and about their Patreon profile, with a humorous admission that he forgot to post the first episode on the platform in a timely manner, which caused laughter in the studio.",

    {
     "subtitle": "Avangarda's return to the studio and a jump in listenership on streaming platforms",
     "screenshot_description": "The hosts and members of the group Avangarda greet each other in the studio at the beginning of the conversation.",
     "content": "After the introductory part, **Khan** announces the special guests – the hip-hop duo **Avangarda**, who are returning to the podcast after more than three and a half years. The host introduces them as some of the current leaders of the domestic *underground* hip-hop scene whose new album has become his personal favorite. The group members arrive at the studio in black outfits, which fit perfectly with **Doktor Oga's** fashion choice.\n\nThe conversation immediately moves in the direction of the new album, which was released on September 10, approximately a month before the filming of the episode. The guests point out that they are extremely satisfied with the initial audience reactions and the growth in listenership on digital platforms. Particularly noteworthy is the data from the **Spotify** service, where the group jumped from 200 to as many as **3700 monthly listeners** in a short period. Although they are satisfied with this initial jump, the guys from **Avangarda** emphasize that they believe the project has the potential for even greater growth.\n\nRecalling their first guest appearance on the podcast, which took place in February or March three and a half years ago, the guests and the host evoke memories of the music video premiere at that time, because of which the episode on YouTube received a monetization ban. The guests explain that work on the new album began approximately half a year after the release of the previous project *Forca*. That period between albums was marked by numerous live performances, as well as learning from their own mistakes, since they did not execute the promotion (*rollout*) for the last album the way they wanted. **Khan** notices that the duo now seems significantly more serious and mature, in which, in his opinion, their producer **Flowdeep** also played a big role, rounding off the whole story at the right moment.",

     "subtitle": "Evolution of sound: Moving away from the Griselda mold towards the energy of the 2000s",
     "screenshot_description": "A guest from Avangarda explains the reasons for the change in sound and the importance of performing songs live.",
     "content": "One of the key topics of the conversation was the musical evolution of the group and a noticeable shift in sound on the new release. **Khan** points out that the album brings something that is chronically lacking on the domestic scene – a sound that carries a certain dose of nostalgia and draws roots from the early 2000s, with smart references that true connoisseurs of hip-hop (*students of the game*) immediately recognize, but without strict copying.\n\nThe guests laughingly reveal an internal agreement before the show according to which one member must talk more because the other, just like his father whom they affectionately call \"Kamerunac\", otherwise takes over every interview. Explaining the conceptual shift, a member of **Avangarda** states that the main turning point was the desire to create songs that work at concerts:\n- The previous project *Forca* had 10 songs, half of which were not suitable for live performance, but for home listening.\n- For the new album, a clear goal was set: **every song must be performable live** in front of an audience.\n- The first album *Propali sportaši 1* was a pure *boom-bap* project through which they wanted to prove their lyrics and skill in putting together multisyllabic rhymes (*multis*) to older colleagues on the scene.\n\nThey also touched upon the popular term \"Griselda sound\" and *drumless* beats (backing tracks without emphasized drums). The guests explain that they, along with the collective **TDK**, were among the first in this region to do such a dirty style while that wave was just starting in the world. Although they consider such a musical backing perfect for beginners and honing the craft on paper because it leaves a lot of room for lyrics and does not require complex melodies, that style no longer attracts them to such an extent. Today, from the American scene, they prefer to listen to artists such as **Roc Marciano** or **Benny the Butcher**, who also stepped outside the box with his latest projects. They conclude that true art requires experimentation and that they did not want to limit another entire album of 12 songs to the same, predictable mold.",

    {
     "subtitle": "From the gym to Oliver Dragojević: A wide spectrum of musical influences",
     "screenshot_description": "Doktor Oga tells how he listened to the entire album for the first time during a workout at the gym.",
     "content": "How dynamic and energetic the new sound of **Avangarda** is is best confirmed by the anecdote of **Doktor Oga**, who reveals that he listened to the album for the first time at the gym on the very morning of its release. The great rhythm and production, credited to **Flowdeep**, proved ideal for training on the bench and treadmill. The guests follow up with a story about their friend who trains MMA and for whom the new album also serves as a perfect background for hitting the bag.\n\nAfter a short humorous digression about how **Doktor Oga** in his \"year without alcohol\" became more tired and of difficult character due to running and training, the conversation returns to the intention behind the sound of the album itself. The members of **Avangarda** point out that they wanted to create a project that sounds equally good in the gym and while driving a car with the windows down – music whose recognizable *bounce* will attract the attention of passersby even if they don't hear the words themselves.\n\nTo **Khan's** question of whether they intensively listened to music from the 2000s during the three years of working on the album to draw inspiration, the guests give a surprising answer:\n- They claim that privately they almost never listen to the genre they are recording at that moment.\n- One of the members reveals that two weeks ago he started chronologically listening to the entire discography of **Oliver Dragojević**, while in other phases he listens exclusively to old rock for a week.\n- Despite this, hip-hop from the 2000s is an inevitable part of their growing up and musical DNA.\n\n**Khan** agrees that the 90s laid the foundations, but the 2000s brought incredible energy through artists such as **50 Cent**, **Chingy**, **Bone Crusher**, **Lil Flip**, and **Three 6 Mafia** – music from which those artists still make a living today, performing at halftimes of competitions like the *Big3* league. The host concludes that after several days of listening to the album on headphones, he came to a clear conclusion: there is currently no such sound in the Balkans at all.",

    {
     "subtitle": "Chemistry of the duo in the studio, perfectionism and the executive role of Flowdeep",
     "screenshot_description": "Khan analyzes the vocal and stylistic dynamics between the two members of Avangarda.",
     "content": "Analyzing the lyrics and vocal performance, the guests explain that they wanted to make a *catchy* album and expand the audience, but without compromise and \"selling out\" in the sense of switching to commercial *dancehall*. They kept their recognizable lyricism, humor, and honesty (*no cap*), paying attention to every line so that it wouldn't happen that in two years they would be ashamed of some verse. As an example of a song that everyone can identify with, they cite *Sirene*, which speaks about the everyday struggle, stress, and getting up at five in the morning for work.\n\n**Khan** especially praises the chemistry between the two rappers, pointing out the verse *\"Brko pulls out revolvers\"* (a reference to the cartoon character Yosemite Sam) as one of the strongest on the album. The host vividly describes their dynamic: one member on the microphone sounds monumental like a giant or a cyclops, while the other provides him with a perfect contrast with his witty and vivid comparisons.\n\nThe guests reveal that this album is the first project on which they worked completely together as a collective, which is why part of the audience often perceives them as \"one man\" (although they joke that one has a pronounced Dalmatian accent, while the other is from Vodice/Zagreb):\n- Unlike previous albums where everyone wrote their 16 bars separately, here they wrote the lyrics together in the apartment.\n- On as many as eight out of twelve songs they share choruses, complement each other, or rap sections written by the other.\n\nThey attribute great credit for the final sound to producer **Flowdeep**, who they say brought out the maximum from them and excelled in all genre variations. Although they enjoyed themselves immensely and had fun during the recording itself, they admit that towards the end of the process stress set in due to their pronounced perfectionism and nitpicking, where months after recording they would question individual lines.",

     "subtitle": "Six months of work on a chorus and a tribute to club hits",
     "screenshot_description": "The guest explains how they wrote and changed choruses for songs on the album for six to eight months.",
     "content": "How dedicated the members of **Avangarda** are to details is best illustrated by the fact that they wrote and recorded the choruses for the songs *Šta ti znaš* and *3.5* for between six and eight months. Through the process, they discarded about ten different variants because they felt it was still not the right thing, until they came to a version that became **Khan's** favorite chorus on the entire album.\n\nOne of the guests admits that he had wanted to try his hand at a more melodic expression for a long time – not classical singing, but specific melodic rapping such as **Khan** himself successfully does on the domestic scene. While their previous darker, *drumless* beats in the style of **Westside Gunn** did not allow such excursions, the new production naturally pulled towards melodic choruses. He was particularly surprised by how relaxed and open the other member of the duo was to such vocal experimentation on this recording.\n\nIn the final part of this block, the conversation touches upon a song that represents a direct tribute (*homage*) to a big hit from the 2000s – the song *SoWhat'ChaSayin'* (or *Do What It Do*) by the singer **Tank**. The guest explains how the idea was born in the studio with **Flowdeep** with the goal of making a tribute to **Tank** and **DJ Paul**.\n\n**Khan** notes that the reinterpretation of old hits is currently a huge trend in America, citing examples of **French Montana** and **Max B**. A member of **Avangarda** emphasizes that when creating that song, the most important thing for him was not to copy the original *flow* nor take the same theme, but to keep only the initial inspiration and give it their authentic signature.",

     "subtitle": "From a whiteboard to unexpected guests: How the collaboration with Krešo Bengalka came about",
     "screenshot_description": "Members of the group Avangarda talk about the exceptional professionalism of Krešo Bengalka during the recording of their joint song.",
     "content": "Selecting guest artists for the new album **Propali sportaši 2** proved to be one of the most demanding tasks in the entire creative process. Host **Khan** pointed out that the hip-hop duo **Avangarda** stepped outside the expected boundaries of their standard crew with this project. Although **Noti Limun** appears on the album, which the audience somewhat expected, the real surprise was the guest appearance of Split rapper **Krešo Bengalka** on the song *Nani*.\n\nThe members of Avangarda revealed that they started the planning process literally in front of an empty whiteboard in their apartment, writing down potential names with a marker and brainstorming for hours about who they could invite to refresh the sound and step outside local frameworks. In the initial combinations for the song *Nani*, they also considered the Serbian artist **TNG**, but his sudden rise in popularity at that moment made realization impossible, so the message with the invitation to collaborate remained only a sent request.\n\nOn the other hand, communication with Krešo Bengalka went flawlessly and beyond all expectations. Although the guests usually prefer personal gatherings over drinks and talking about life before entering the studio — which is easily doable with the Zagreb crew — distance dictated a different approach. There was mild skepticism about whether Krešo had even heard of their previous work, but the Split rapper showed top-notch professionalism. He liked the song on the first listen, and within just two days he sent the recorded material. Instead of the standard 16 bars, Krešo \"treated\" them to as many as 24 top-notch verses, thereby once again justifying his reputation as an artist who regularly excels on guest tracks.\n\nFor the Split member of Avangarda, this collaboration also had a special emotional weight. He revealed an interesting detail that he and Krešo grew up in the same Split neighborhood — **Split 3**, just a few streets apart, below Visoka, which gave the whole story additional authenticity.",

     "subtitle": "The cult status of Kiša metaka and the T-shirt ruined by acetone",
     "screenshot_description": "The guest laughingly recounts the anecdote with the ruined Kiša metaka T-shirt and the falling acetone in the bathroom.",
     "content": "The conversation about Krešo Bengalka naturally opened up the topic of the immense influence that the cult Split group **Kiša metaka** left on the members of Avangarda. Both guests — both the Split native and the Zagreb native in the duo — agreed that this very collective was the key trigger for their entry into the world of rap, admitting that without the influence of Kiša metaka they probably would never have started making music. After the realized collaboration with Krešo, the guests jokingly, but also with a serious desire, said that their next big goal is to record a song with **Vojko V**, which would round off their boyhood dreams.\n\nHow deep this connection is is best illustrated by an anecdote from 2013, when the Split member of Avangarda had just moved to **Zagreb**. At that time, during a concert at **KSET**, he ordered the first series of promotional Kiša metaka T-shirts. He recalled that it was a completely different era in which Vojko V personally called him on his mobile phone to locate him and hand him the ordered T-shirt.\n\nHowever, that valuable piece of *merch* experienced a bizarre fate. While the guest was showering and getting ready to go out, he left the T-shirt next to the toilet bowl. At that moment, his mother's nail acetone fell from the shelf above the sink, bounced off the edge of the washbasin, and spilled right onto the black T-shirt, permanently damaging it. Although hosts **Khan** and **Doktor Oga** laughingly asked him to \"spice up\" the story a bit with more dramatic details for the needs of the podcast, the guest revealed that he still keeps that T-shirt today — pulled over the back of a chair in his apartment, so he can see it every time he comes home from work.",

     "screenshot_description": "The moment in the studio when, upon opening a can, the beer foams up and spills on the table.",
     "content": "The relaxed atmosphere in the studio warmed up further during the tasting of domestic craft beers from the **Pomalo** brewery. While host **Doktor Oga**, due to his year-long abstinence from alcohol, remained faithful to non-alcoholic cocktails — with joking comments from the crew about what his return to alcohol will look like in the first days of the new year — the rest of the table moved on to tasting beer.\n\nAlthough one of the guests from Avangarda is not usually a fan of craft brewing and prefers classic beers from two-liter bottles like **Löwenbräu**, he was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the offered drink. The mention of the cult \"sow\" [two-liter bottle] of Löwenbräu sparked a wave of nostalgia and memories of high school days, graduation parades, and first serious drunkenness.\n\nKhan recalled his graduation and the celebration in Zagreb's **Maksimir** park, where warm Löwenbräu was drunk as early as nine o'clock in the morning in the greatest heat, resulting in all-day nausea. Building on stories about youthful experiments with alcohol, the participants listed drinks they can no longer even look at today:\n- **Vigor vodka** with various fruit flavors\n- **Tequila** and overly sweet margaritas\n- Cheap red wines for *bambus* [red wine and cola] such as **Vranac**, **Venus**, and the infamous **Ribar** in a carton or bag, from which, as they say, the mornings were particularly critical.\n\nThe discussion about alcohol culminated in a comical moment when one of the guests tried to open a new can of beer, which due to shaking erupted into a real foamy fountain right in the middle of the studio table.",

     "content": "After cleaning up the spilled beer from the table, the members of **Avangarda** used the opportunity to hand out special gifts to the hosts. **Khan** and **Doktor Oga** received black T-shirts from the first, strictly limited promotional collection of the new album. The guests explained that the entire series was sold out in record time, but they intentionally saved the last two copies on the side specifically for the podcast hosts.\n\nThe hosts did not hide their enthusiasm for the quality of workmanship. Khan特に praised the cut and material, highlighting the details that make a difference:\n- A firm, thicker, and high-quality collar around the neck\n- Heavy, high-grammage cotton\n- Durable print that won't easily peel off during washing\n- Modern *oversized* cut.\n\nThe group members revealed that for this first *drop* they printed exactly **30 pieces** exclusively for the needs of promoting the album. Their goal was to create true exclusivity, so that the most loyal fans who supported the project right from the start would have a unique piece of clothing that will still have collector's value in ten years. Of course, given the previously told trauma from the bathroom, the T-shirts came with a strict warning to the hosts to keep them away from acetone.",

     "subtitle": "Stepping out of the chamber of secrets: Why people outside the hip-hop world listened to the new album first",
     "screenshot_description": "Members of Avangarda explain how during the recording of the third album they sent working versions of songs to friends who do not listen to rap.",
     "content": "One of the biggest changes in the approach to working on the third project was openness to outside opinions during the creation process itself. While they kept the first two releases in strict secrecy — like a \"chamber of secrets\", fearing that someone outside the circle might hear an unfinished song — with the album **Propali sportaši 2** they applied a completely opposite strategy. From the first recorded track, they sent demos to family, relatives, and a wide circle of friends.\n\nThey placed special focus on friends and acquaintances who do not listen to rap at all nor follow the domestic scene. The guests explained that the most valuable thing to them was precisely that unfiltered *feedback* from people who divide music exclusively into good and bad, regardless of genre. While certain acquaintances used to brutally honestly comment on the first albums as too dark or heavy for everyday listening, asking for something that \"bangs in the car or the gym\", the reactions to the new songs were unanimously positive.\n\nWhen they realized that people completely outside the hip-hop world liked the material, while at the same time maintaining a high level of lyrics appreciated by their home crew and the collective **TRK**, they knew they had a winning formula. Even younger colleagues from the scene gave huge support to the change in sound, without any objections for moving away from the classic *boom bap* or *Griselda* style.",

     "subtitle": "Flowdeep as executive producer and Noti Limun as a new reinforcement in Dubrava",
     "screenshot_description": "Conversation about the role of producer Flowdeep in shaping the final sound of the album and selecting instrumentals.",
     "content": "The final part of the conversation about the anatomy of the album itself was dedicated to the instrumental backing and the remaining collaborators. Host **Khan** singled out the song *Taj lik* (featuring **Noti Limun**), declaring its musical backing one of the three best *beats* he has heard in the current year. The members of Avangarda revealed that this instrumental is signed by producer **prod.by.sone**, while the remaining external backing track on the album was done by **Ivanov**, and everything else is the work of their main collaborator **Flowdeep**.\n\nIt is interesting that it was Flowdeep who found Sone's *beat* for the song *Taj lik* and insisted they take it for the album. By doing so, he actually took on the role of a true executive producer (*executive producer*) of the entire project. His authority and vision were crucial in many moments — the guests admitted that for the song *Sirene* they had already chosen another instrumental that they liked, but Flowdeep assessed that it was not good enough and directed them towards another solution. He also showed his quality control by placing a \"veto\" on one potential guest appearance that they badly wanted to realize.\n\nTouching upon Noti Limun himself — who, having heard the *beat* for *Taj lik* still in the early phase of recording, immediately reserved his spot on that track — a local exclusive was also revealed in the studio. Noti Limun recently moved to Zagreb's **Dubrava**, more precisely to **Retkovec** (Poljanice).      "subtitle": "Performance at the Garden and Rigz's late arrival: A true block party atmosphere",
     "screenshot_description": "Members of the group Avangarda explain how the performance at the Garden went and why they went on stage before the main guest",
     "content": "The conversation shifted to the recently held traditional hip-hop event which this year, after previous editions in Močvara and Vintage, was moved outdoors for the first time – to the Garden venue. Host Khan pointed out that the guys from the group Avangarda were the domestic flagships and co-headliners of the evening alongside the foreign guest, American rapper Rigz, whom Khan honestly admitted he hadn't followed before the announcement until producer Flowdeep introduced him to his work.\n\nThe members of Avangarda expressed their enthusiasm for the location itself and the warm September weather that allowed for a relaxed outdoor gathering. However, they looked back on the organizational challenges related to the main guest. As they explained, bringing foreign artists is an excellent move for raising the entire Zagreb and Croatian scene to a higher level, but Rigz's performance was marked by a delay:\n\n- The American rapper was an hour and a half late to the event.\n- Although according to the plan Avangarda was supposed to perform after him as the closing act of the evening, due to the delay and last-minute agreements, Rigz asked for the domestic duo to go out first.\n- The members of Avangarda even waited to go on stage so that the audience would gather and to give him a proper welcome, but when they finished their energetic set, a large part of the audience that came primarily for them retreated towards the bar and the exit, so Rigz ended up performing in front of a significantly smaller number of people than could have been.\n\nDespite that oversight with the schedule, the guests praised the overall concept of the event. They pointed out that no one had made such a real *block party* in Zagreb for a long time – alongside the concerts themselves, visitors could enjoy graffiti drawing, table football, table tennis, T-shirt stands, and exhibited works, which created a sense of a true hip-hop community and culture in one place.",
